subject: Reserved SKU mix and burst-tier protection — ask for capped GPU pass-through
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Celeste Alvarez <celeste@luminary.ai>, procurement@luminary.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved SKU mix and burst-tier protection — ask for capped GPU pass-through

Hi Celeste / Luminary procurement team,

Thanks again for walking through the Dedicated sizing last week. To keep our Q3 onboarding timeline aligned, we want to propose the reserved SKU mix and a guardrail we think will make a larger commit acceptable on both sides.

Summary of ask (short):
- Commit: reserved capacity (Aurora-P / 8xA100 equiv) for 12 months starting 2026-07-01.
- Pricing protection: a capped GPU pass-through that limits Luminary’s exposure to abrupt market price spikes.
- Mechanism proposed: if a public GPU cost index (attached) rises >20% vs baseline, Redwood provides a credit sleeve up to 10% of monthly invoice and opens a review window for rebalancing reserved SKUs.

Why this helps: it lets Luminary lock predictable baseline throughput for product launch while giving you a bounded remediation when wholesale GPU costs materially spike. For Redwood it keeps utilization stable and allows us to price predictably for committed pools.

Attached: commit_terms_draft.pdf (initial redline) and gpu_price_index_sheet.xlsx (baseline & trigger definition).

Request: can procurement confirm (1) this structure is acceptable in principle, (2) if you prefer % thresholds other than 20%/10% (we can be flexible), and (3) whether your legal team needs an alternate clause for index source (we proposed CloudExchange index).

Next steps: if you approve in principle, I’ll loop in our finance ops lead (Marcus) for any exec signoff depending on the credit cap value.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 30-min sync to walk numbers.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

Attachments: commit_terms_draft.pdf, gpu_price_index_sheet.xlsx
From: Celeste Alvarez <celeste@luminary.ai>

Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved SKU mix and burst-tier protection — ask for capped GPU pass-through

Hi Mateo — thanks for the note and the documents. A few clarifying items from procurement / finance before we escalate to legal: 

1) Can you provide an example billing table that shows how the credit sleeve would apply across a month with a 25% index spike? We need to see line-level math.
2) How frequently would the index be sampled? Daily, weekly, monthly? We prefer monthly sampling but want to understand volatility smoothing.
3) If prices fall, do we get any retroactive adjustment? (i.e., symmetrical passage or only protection on spikes)

We have an internal guidance limit on contingency credits of 12% of monthly burn for a single vendor without VP approval. If your proposal needs >12% we will need Marcus or a finance executive in the loop.

Can you send the example table and suggested sampling cadence? Also, we will require SOC2/Audit evidence (we have that on file from Redwood but will confirm).

Thanks — Celeste
Celeste Alvarez
Head of Cloud Procurement, Luminary AI
celeste@luminary.ai
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Reserved SKU mix and burst-tier protection — Luminary ask (credit cap vs procurement limit)

Marcus — forwarding the procurement thread from Luminary. Short version: they like the structure but note an internal cap of 12% contingency credit without VP approval. Our proposal (attached) sets a 10% monthly credit sleeve when their chosen GPU index spikes >20% vs baseline.

Ask: can you confirm approval for up to a 10% monthly credit sleeve on a 12-month reserved commit (Deal ID DEAL-4729)? If you prefer, we can propose a staggered ladder (5% up to 15% index change, 10% up to 30%) instead of a single fixed sleeve.

Why this is time-sensitive: Luminary's launch calendar needs contract signed by 2026-05-05 to reserve capacity and meet hardware lead times. Losing that window means pushing start to Q4 and creates both revenue and capacity planning friction.

Attachments: redline_commit_terms_v2.pdf (shows credit clause and index definition).

Thanks — Mateo
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Reserved SKU mix and burst-tier protection — Luminary ask (credit cap vs procurement limit)

Thanks for the context — quick internal analysis and recommendation.

Summary of GPU-cost sensitivity (short):
- Baseline unit cost (our internal A100 equiv): $3.20 / hour equivalent (contract baseline).
- Historical 12-month volatility (CloudExchange index): mean +/- 14%.
- Stress scenario (supply shock): +35% for 6 weeks observed in 2024.

Options and recommended path:
1) Approve a fixed 10% monthly credit sleeve with monthly sampling and a 20% trigger. Pros: easy to administer, buyer-friendly, preserves our committed pool economics for normal months. Cons: tail risk if index stays elevated for multiple months.
2) Approve a 3-tier ladder (recommended):
   - Tier A: index rise 10-19% -> 4% credit (monthly);
   - Tier B: index rise 20-29% -> 8% credit (monthly);
   - Tier C: index rise >=30% -> 12% credit (monthly, but requires VP finance quick-approval to enable).
   This keeps us within typical procurement caps while giving Luminary protection; it bounds our downside and creates a manual approval step for extreme tails.
3) Alternative: cap-duration approach — 10% credit but capped to two months per 12-month term (reduces exposure).

Operational notes:
- Index sampling: use monthly average of CloudExchange index; align baseline to the first full month preceding contract signature.
- Retroactive adjustments: avoid retroactive refunds for index drops (one-way protection only) — simpler for invoicing and dispute avoidance.
- Accounting: we should book an expected credit reserve when ramping; finance to confirm earnout treatment.

Recommendation: option 2 (3-tier ladder) with Tier C requiring VP sign-off. This conforms with Luminary's stated 12% internal limit and preserves a clear escape hatch for us at extreme tails.

If Marcus signs off, I'll draft a short executable clause for the SOW and update the redline.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Strategy, Redwood Inference
